items.title: Patel: From Barrister to 'Sardar'
items.body:
## Early life & entry into the movement

- **Vallabhbhai Patel** (b. 1875, Nadiad, Gujarat) qualified as a **barrister in London** and built a successful legal practice in **Ahmedabad**.
- Drawn into the freedom struggle by **Gandhi**, he abandoned his practice for the national cause.

## The satyagrahas that made him

- **Kheda Satyagraha (1918)** — his first mass campaign, alongside Gandhi, seeking suspension of land revenue after crop failure and plague.
- **Bardoli Satyagraha (1928)** — organised peasants of Bardoli (Surat) against a steep (~22%) revenue enhancement; disciplined non-payment forced the government to **roll back** the hike and release confiscated land.
- The women of Bardoli honoured him with the title **'Sardar'** (leader), which stuck for life.

## Role in the Congress

- A superb **organiser and disciplinarian**, Patel was the Congress's chief fund-raiser and machine-builder, and a member of its highest councils through the 1930s–40s.
keyPoints: Vallabhbhai Patel (b. 1875, Nadiad) was a London-trained barrister who joined the struggle under Gandhi.
Kheda Satyagraha (1918) was his first mass campaign against land revenue during crop failure.
Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) forced a rollback of a ~22% revenue hike.
The women of Bardoli gave him the title 'Sardar' after the 1928 success.
He was the Congress's foremost organiser and disciplinarian.
items.mnemonic: Order of Patel's campaigns: 'KB' = Kheda (1918) before Bardoli (1928).
items.source: NCERT & Britannica — Vallabhbhai Patel; Kheda & Bardoli Satyagrahas

items.title: Iron Man: Integration of the Princely States
items.body:
## The problem in 1947

- With the lapse of **British paramountcy**, about **565 princely states** were technically free to join **India**, join **Pakistan**, or stay **independent** — threatening the balkanisation of India.

## Patel's machinery

- As head of the new **States Department** (created July 1947), Patel — assisted by Secretary **V.P. Menon** — combined **persuasion, appeals to patriotism and firmness** to bring rulers in.
- Instrument used: the **Instrument of Accession**, by which a state ceded only **defence, external affairs and communications** to the Union, plus a **Standstill Agreement** for continuity.
- Rulers who acceded were assured **privy purses** and retention of privileges (later abolished in 1971).

## Outcome

- By 15 August 1947 the **vast majority** of states had signed; the handful of hold-outs (Junagadh, Hyderabad, Kashmir) were resolved by 1948–49.
- For welding a fragmented map into one Union, Patel earned the epithets **'Iron Man of India'** and **'Bismarck of India'**.
keyPoints: About 565 princely states were free to join India, join Pakistan, or stay independent in 1947.
Patel headed the States Department (1947), assisted by Secretary V.P. Menon.
The Instrument of Accession ceded defence, external affairs and communications to the Union.
Acceding rulers were promised privy purses (abolished in 1971).
Patel's success earned him the titles 'Iron Man' and 'Bismarck' of India.
items.source: NCERT 'Politics in India Since Independence' & Britannica — integration of princely states

items.title: The Three Hard Cases: Junagadh, Hyderabad, Kashmir
items.body:
## The states that resisted

Most states acceded peacefully; three required special handling.

| State | Ruler & problem | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| **Junagadh** | Muslim Nawab acceded to Pakistan despite Hindu-majority population and no land link | **Plebiscite (Feb 1948)** overwhelmingly chose India |
| **Hyderabad** | Nizam sought independence; Razakar militia violence | **Operation Polo / Police Action (Sept 1948)** integrated it |
| **Jammu & Kashmir** | Maharaja Hari Singh hesitated; Pakistani tribal invasion (Oct 1947) | Signed the **Instrument of Accession (26 Oct 1947)**; India sent troops |

## Points to remember

- **Travancore** and **Bhopal** also flirted with independence but soon acceded.
- Kashmir's accession, made under Article 370's special arrangement, remained politically contentious.
keyPoints: Junagadh: Nawab acceded to Pakistan; a February 1948 plebiscite chose India.
Hyderabad: integrated by Operation Polo (Police Action) in September 1948.
Jammu & Kashmir: Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947 after a tribal invasion.
Travancore and Bhopal briefly sought independence before acceding.
These three were the main exceptions to otherwise peaceful accession.
items.mnemonic: Trouble trio 'J-H-K' = Junagadh (plebiscite), Hyderabad (Operation Polo), Kashmir (Instrument of Accession).
items.source: NCERT & Britannica — Junagadh, Hyderabad, Kashmir accession

items.title: Patel in Free India & His Legacy
items.body:
## Office

- Patel was independent India's **first Home Minister** and **Deputy Prime Minister**, also holding the **States** and **Information & Broadcasting** portfolios.

## The 'steel frame'

- In the **Constituent Assembly** he championed retaining the **All India Services**, calling them the **'steel frame'** that would keep the Union together; he is regarded as the **patron of the modern IAS/IPS**.

## Death & commemoration

- Patel died in **December 1950**; he was posthumously awarded the **Bharat Ratna in 1991**.
- The **Statue of Unity** (182 m, at Kevadia, Gujarat; the world's tallest statue, inaugurated 2018) is dedicated to him.
- His birth anniversary, **31 October**, is observed as **Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day)**.
keyPoints: Patel was India's first Home Minister and Deputy PM, also handling States and I&B.
He defended the All India Services as the 'steel frame' of India in the Constituent Assembly.
He died in December 1950 and received the Bharat Ratna (posthumous) in 1991.
The Statue of Unity (182 m, Kevadia, Gujarat) is the world's tallest statue.
31 October is observed as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day).
items.source: Government of India & Britannica — Vallabhbhai Patel; Statue of Unity; National Unity Day

items.title: Bose's Rise in the Congress & the Tripuri Split
items.body:
## From Deshbandhu's protégé to Congress President

- **Subhas Chandra Bose** (b. 1897, Cuttack) resigned from the **ICS** to join the freedom struggle, becoming a protégé of **Chittaranjan Das (Deshbandhu)** in Bengal.
- A leader of the Congress **left wing**, he was elected President at the **Haripura Session (1938)**, backing rapid industrialisation and a **National Planning Committee**.

## The Tripuri crisis (1939)

- At **Tripuri (1939)** Bose won re-election by defeating **Pattabhi Sitaramayya**, whom Gandhi had backed; Gandhi called it **'more my defeat than his'**.
- Facing a non-cooperative Congress Working Committee, Bose **resigned** the presidency.

## The Forward Bloc

- In **1939** he founded the **Forward Bloc** to consolidate **left and radical elements** within the Congress for an uncompromising struggle.
keyPoints: Bose (b. 1897, Cuttack) resigned the ICS and became a protégé of C.R. Das in Bengal.
Elected Congress President at Haripura (1938), backing planning and industrialisation.
At Tripuri (1939) he defeated Gandhi's candidate Pattabhi Sitaramayya, then resigned.
Gandhi called Sitaramayya's defeat 'more my defeat than his'.
He founded the Forward Bloc in 1939 to unite Congress's left wing.
items.mnemonic: Bose's two chairs: 'HT' = Haripura (1938) then Tripuri (1939).
items.source: NCERT & Britannica — Subhas Chandra Bose; Haripura & Tripuri sessions

items.title: Netaji: Escape, the INA & Azad Hind
items.body:
## The Great Escape (1941)

- Under house arrest in Calcutta, Bose **escaped in 1941**, reaching **Germany via Afghanistan and the USSR**, where he raised the **Free India Legion** and set up a **Free India Centre**.
- In **1943** he made a **submarine voyage** (German U-boat to a Japanese submarine) to reach **Southeast Asia**.

## The Indian National Army

- The **INA (Azad Hind Fauj)** was first raised from Indian PoWs by **Mohan Singh (1942)** and **revived and reorganised by Bose in 1943**.
- Its women's wing was the **Rani of Jhansi Regiment**, led by **Capt. Lakshmi Sahgal**.
- The INA fought alongside Japan and reached Indian soil, hoisting the flag at **Moirang, Manipur (1944)**.

## Azad Hind Government & legacy

- Bose proclaimed the **Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind)** at **Singapore (Oct 1943)**, recognised by several Axis powers.
- Slogans: **'Give me blood, and I will give you freedom'**, **'Jai Hind'**; he is revered as **'Netaji'**.
- He is reported to have **died in an air crash at Taihoku (Taipei) in August 1945**; his birthday, **23 January**, is observed as **Parakram Diwas**.
keyPoints: Bose escaped house arrest in 1941 and reached Germany, raising the Free India Legion.
In 1943 he travelled by submarine to Southeast Asia and revived the INA (first raised by Mohan Singh, 1942).
The Rani of Jhansi Regiment (women's wing) was led by Capt. Lakshmi Sahgal.
The INA hoisted the Indian flag at Moirang, Manipur, in 1944.
Bose proclaimed the Azad Hind Government at Singapore in October 1943.
Slogans 'Give me blood…' and 'Jai Hind'; reported to have died in a 1945 Taihoku air crash; 23 January is Parakram Diwas.
items.mnemonic: Bose's route 'G-J': Germany then Japan/Southeast Asia (by submarine, 1943).
items.source: Britannica & Government of India — Subhas Chandra Bose; INA; Azad Hind Government

items.title: INA Trials, Rash Behari Bose & PYQ Specials
items.body:
## Rash Behari Bose & the founding of the INA

- **Rash Behari Bose** (Ghadar/revolutionary veteran in Japan) helped establish the first INA and the **Indian Independence League**; he formally **handed over INA leadership to Subhas Chandra Bose on 4 July 1943** at Singapore.

## INA campaigns

- The INA fought alongside the Japanese at **Imphal and Kohima (1944)** and hoisted the flag at **Moirang, Manipur**.

## The INA (Red Fort) Trials, 1945

- After Japan's surrender, captured INA officers were court-martialled at the **Red Fort, Delhi (Nov 1945)**.
- The famous first trial was of the trio **Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Kumar Sahgal (Sehgal) and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon** (deliberately one Hindu, one Muslim, one Sikh).
- Defence counsel included **Bhulabhai Desai, Jawaharlal Nehru, Tej Bahadur Sapru and K.N. Katju**; the trials sparked mass sympathy and the **RIN Mutiny (1946)**.

## Patel — Karachi Session (1931)

- **Sardar Patel presided over the Karachi Session of the Congress (1931)**, which endorsed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact and adopted the resolution on **Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme**.

## Commemoration

- The **Andaman & Nicobar Islands** were renamed to honour the INA — including **Ross Island → Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep**, and **Neil & Havelock → Shaheed & Swaraj Dweep**.
keyPoints: Rash Behari Bose founded the first INA/Indian Independence League and handed leadership to S.C. Bose on 4 July 1943.
INA fought at Imphal & Kohima (1944) and hoisted the flag at Moirang, Manipur.
INA (Red Fort) Trials, Nov 1945: Shah Nawaz Khan, P.K. Sahgal and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon (Hindu-Muslim-Sikh trio).
Defence counsel: Bhulabhai Desai, Nehru, Tej Bahadur Sapru, K.N. Katju; trials fed the 1946 RIN Mutiny.
Patel presided over the Congress Karachi Session (1931) — Fundamental Rights & National Economic Programme resolution.
Andaman islands renamed: Ross → Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep; Neil & Havelock → Shaheed & Swaraj Dweep.
items.mnemonic: INA trio at Red Fort = one each Hindu-Muslim-Sikh: Sahgal, Shah Nawaz Khan, Dhillon.
items.source: Standard references — INA Red Fort trials; Rash Behari Bose; Karachi Session 1931; Andaman renaming
